greeting: Hi — I'm the front desk at Studio 1973. Ask me what the studio makes, what things cost, where we are, or why it's called 1973.

fallback.a: Great question — that one deserves a proper answer from the team rather than a canned one from me. Tune the television below to channel 3 and send it through; the studio reads everything.

entries.a: Interactive websites, AI assistants like me, and full platforms — designed, built, and shipped under one roof. Plus photography, which sneaks into everything.

Pricing depends on the shape of the thing — a site, an assistant, and a full platform are different animals, and honest numbers need a real conversation. Send a line through the television below and you'll get a straight answer, fast.
The studio is based near Canberra, Australia — and works with people everywhere. Most projects run entirely online, time zones permitting (and sometimes despite them).

Distance isn't a problem — the studio builds for the open web and works with clients wherever they are. Everything from kickoff to launch happens online, so the only thing we'll negotiate is meeting times.

It depends on the build, but the studio ships quickly and without ceremony — simpler sites in weeks, platforms in phases. Share your deadline through the contact form and you'll get an honest read on what fits.

It starts with a conversation: what you need, who it's for, what done looks like. Then the studio designs, builds, and ships — the same hands the whole way through, no hand-offs. Channel 3 on the television below is the front door.

Scroll up to the work section: hear.is, an acoustic accessibility map; Listing Lens, a second opinion on any car listing; and Santa's Secret, a bricks-and-mortar Christmas shop in Bungendore whose website snows. Client work is taken by invitation — say hello and see.

hear.is is an acoustic accessibility map — you record 15 seconds of a place and it describes what it sounds like, for blind, low-vision and sensory-sensitive visitors. The raw audio never leaves your phone; the description is written from abstract descriptors only.

saygday.ai is the studio's own chatbot platform — friendly AI assistants for real businesses, built with an Australian accent. Its first shop floor is Santa's Secret in Bungendore, and there's more coming. Watch this space.

Listing Lens (listinglens.app) is a studio platform in the workshop: screenshot any online vehicle listing and it builds a full report — recalls, known faults, owner experiences, the genuine positives — then arms you with the questions to ask the seller before any money moves.

The studio's latest client build is Santa's Secret — Kim's bricks-and-mortar Christmas shop in Bungendore, NSW, half an hour from Canberra. Handcrafted ornaments, custom trees, 'an unconventional Christmas' — so the site got its own falling snow (look for the snowy card in the work section) and a front-of-house AI assistant. Live at santasecret.com.au.

1973 is the founder's birth year — and the year the Xerox Alto, Ethernet, and the first mobile phone call all arrived. A good vintage for someone who builds on the web, hence Studio 1973. Every project ships with a 'made in 1973' mark in its footer.

Photography is the studio's oldest habit — older than the web. Scroll to the darkroom section and hold your pointer on a frame: it develops, just like a print under the enlarger. It sneaks into client work too.

Assistants like this one are a studio speciality — grounded in your business, front of house on your own site, shipped on saygday.ai. The first is already greeting customers at Santa's Secret. Ask for one through the television below.

The studio doesn't ship and vanish — sites launch with everything they need to stay fast, secure, and current, and ongoing care is part of the conversation. Raise it when you get in touch and we'll shape it to the build.
Studio 1973 is a small independent studio — senior hands on every project, no account managers in between. The same team that answers the email designs the thing, builds the thing, and ships it.
Scroll down to the television set and tune it to channel 3 — the contact form is broadcasting there, straight to the studio. Small studio, short queue, honest answers.

Every site and platform the studio ships carries a small 'made in 1973' mark in its footer — a quiet, consistent signature that links back home. Scroll to the signature section to see it on both light and dark.
G'day! Ask me what the studio makes, what things cost, where we are — or how to get something of your own built.
Any time. If you'd like to take it further, the television below is broadcasting the contact form on channel 3.
